subject: Sprint-to-close: proposed accelerated stabilization and re-baseline
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Park <kelly.park@brightspark.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: MAP and evaluation plan proposal — BrightSpark / Redwood

Kelly — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan that lays out the core milestones (eval, security review, procurement, and pilot). The key asks from your side were: access for a 2-week eval, SOC/attestation pointers, and procurement timing.

High level proposal (attached: BrightSpark-MAP-v1.3.xlsx):
- Week 1: credentials + test dataset ingest, smoke tests
- Week 2: focused eval on 3 KPIs (latency, throughput, query-relevance) using our EvalPlan testsuite
- Week 3: security sign-off and SOW/terms finalization
- Week 4: pilot kickoff (30-day pilot)

Two asks from you to keep this timeline: confirm procurement timelines (who signs SOW) and permission to run the subset of production-like queries for the eval. If procurement is slower, we should identify the minimal evaluation slice we can run without a signed SOW so BrightSpark can still land on a baseline before procurement clears.

Attaching: BrightSpark-MAP-v1.3.xlsx

Thanks — I can be flexible with start dates, but I'd like to keep the close target in Feb if possible.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference — Production-grade inference for engineering teams

From: Kelly Park <kelly.park@brightspark.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and evaluation plan proposal — BrightSpark / Redwood

Aisha — thanks for the prep and clear MAP. We like the structure, but a quick heads up: procurement just told me our standard SOW turnaround is 3–4 weeks (they require a vendor questionnaire and fiscal review). That will push the sign step.

Options from our side:
- Procurement will prioritize if we have legal/finance boilerplate up front, but they still need approvals (likely by Jan 28)
- We could run a constrained eval earlier (non-prod subset) but security will need written scope; does Redwood have a temporary eval agreement or short-term data processing addendum we can use?

I can try to accelerate but I don’t want to overpromise. If we can show pilot readiness before procurement completes, that would help our internal case.

— Kelly
Kelly Park | Head of Data Science, BrightSpark Analytics
kelly.park@brightspark.ai | +1 (617) 555-8421

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: MAP and evaluation plan proposal — BrightSpark / Redwood — procurement slip (internal)

Folks — forwarding Kelly's note. Procurement delay is likely to push our close by ~2–3 weeks unless we enable a constrained eval path. Proposed mitigation plan and asks below (I’ll own coordination):

Mitigation options (priority order):
1) Offer a 2-week constrained eval on anonymized subset under NDA + temporary DPA/limited scope addendum. This lets BrightSpark validate latency and relevance without full SOW. (Client agreed in principle if we can provide the addendum.)
2) Provide a pre-signed SOW template + exhibit with clear acceptance criteria to speed internal approvals. Legal to confirm minimal commercial edits (Ben / Priyom to weigh in).
3) Offer 10% credit on pilot invoices if procurement timing causes a >14 day slip from target close — managerial approval required.

Operational asks:
- Marissa: can we compress the eval tests to a 3-metric baseline (latency P95, query throughput, top-5 relevance) and run a stripped-down suite? I’ll attach the testsuite (EvalPlan-testsuite.zip stub).
- Priyom: confirm whether we can enable a short-lived account with anonymized dataset under an NDA without legal pushback. If not, what minimum language do we need?
- Ben: need quick sign-off on a discretionary credit and on us circulating a pre-filled SOW to procurement.

Risk log (high level):
- Cause: procurement cadence & vendor questionnaire
- Impact: close-date slip; potential loss of priority from exec sponsor
- Contingency: constrained eval + pre-filled SOW + discretionary credit

I’ll draft the updated MAP and SOW and send to Kelly by Monday.

— Aisha
(On Wed, Jan 13, 2027 at 10:14 AM Kelly Park <kelly.park@brightspark.ai> wrote:)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP and evaluation plan proposal — BrightSpark / Redwood — procurement slip (internal)

Thanks for the heads up, Aisha. I support the constrained eval route and distributing a pre-filled SOW to procurement — those are low-friction ways to keep momentum.

On credits: approve up to 10% on pilot invoice as a discretionary concession for procurement delays; I’ll authorize that provided we get a manager-signed exception and the credit is time-bound (applies only if procurement pushes baseline >14 days). Priyom / Legal, please prepare the short exception form.

Also cc’ing Marissa: please work with Aisha on the compressed eval plan and ensure our telemetry captures the three KPIs (latency P95, throughput at X qps, relevance top-5). We want data to surface in the Console dashboard so execs can see progress.

— Ben

Subject: Updated MAP + constrained eval path and re-baseline proposal

Kelly — attached are three items we discussed: updated MAP (BrightSpark-MAP-v1.3.xlsx), compressed EvalPlan (EvalPlan-testsuite.zip stub) and a draft SOW (SOW-draft-v2.docx). Summary of changes: 

- Re-baseline proposal:
  • Start constrained eval: Jan 25–Feb 7 (2 weeks) — anonymized subset under NDA
  • Security checklist and vendor questionnaire: BrightSpark completes by Jan 28
  • Final SOW execution target: Feb 8 (procurement permitting)
  • Pilot kickoff (30-day): Feb 9–Mar 10

- Contingency / Escalation:
  • If procurement extends beyond Feb 8, Redwood will provide a 10% pilot credit (per Ben's approval) and weekly stakeholder check-ins until SOW signs.
  • We’ll run the compressed eval first to generate objective telemetry and expedite executive approval.

Doc links: DocuSign pre-fill (https://www.docusign.com/en/link/signer?envelopeId=ENVELOPE-98765) — feel free to share with procurement to quicken approvals.

Please confirm if the Jan 25 start for the constrained eval works for your team and whether procurement needs any additional artifacts. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with procurement/legal this week to unblock.

Best — Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Procurement will circulate vendor questionnaire by EOD today to the Redwood legal contact on the DocuSign pre-fill
- Security will review the EvalPlan (you attached) and provide a short list of gating items by Jan 22

We’re good to proceed with the re-baseline as laid out. Please schedule weekly 30-minute check-ins (Fri at 11am PT) starting Jan 29 — I’ll include procurement and security on calls as needed.
